expectations.name: s4_warns
expectations.detail: triggering event (relay_edge {'relay': 'K1', 'edge': 'close'}) never occurred [BLOCKED: RESOLVED on the SaftyFW side, still blocked on the fixture. The old reason here -- 'context_valid is never set true by safety_core_build_input()' -- was fixed by commit f304392: context_valid, any_current_present and relay_commanded_continuously are all populated for real now, and virtual_dut confirms context_valid is true on every poll of this scenario. S4 is therefore EVALUATED every tick; it simply never warns, because `relay_commanded_continuously && !any_current_present` needs a relay commanded on continuously for correlation_window_s (150s) and no relay ever closes in a virtual_dut run: there is no KilnFW/PID in the loop to close K1, and this scenario's own `relay_edge K1 close` trigger never occurs for the same reason (the clause reports 'triggering event never occurred', not a guard verdict).]

blocked_on.phase: Not a SaftyFW phase gap any more. The remaining gap is SimFW-side: nothing in the fixture ever commands a zone relay on, so S4's positive half cannot be presented. Closing it needs either a virtual KilnFW/PID that drives K1..K3, or a scenario that forces a relay closed independently of heat (welded_relay-class faults already exist but are triggered on zone temperatures this fixture never reaches while K4 gates duty). See firmware/SimFW/tools/virtual_dut/README.md.

expectations.name: s4_never_trips
expectations.detail: dut:K4_open observed before the boundary (first at seq 2000000000) [BLOCKED: This forbid clause is still satisfied for the wrong reason: K4 is open at sim-time 0 and never closes, so it is already true before anything under test has had a chance to say otherwise. NOTE (updated after SaftyFW commit f304392): the previous wording here -- 'relay_owner_command_energize() is called by nothing in the current source tree' -- is no longer true. It now has a caller, safety_core_request_enable(), reached from link_task.c's SAFETY_CMD_REQUEST_ENABLE (0x02) decoder. That path is driven only by an explicit operator/PC command (KilnFW's uart_bridge.c -> safety_link_request_enable(), i.e. PcTools' safety_request_enable MCP tool); KilnFW does NOT request enable automatically when a profile runs, and no scenario in this library models that operator step.]

blocked_on.reason: This forbid clause is still satisfied for the wrong reason: K4 is open at sim-time 0 and never closes, so it is already true before anything under test has had a chance to say otherwise. NOTE (updated after SaftyFW commit f304392): the previous wording here -- 'relay_owner_command_energize() is called by nothing in the current source tree' -- is no longer true. It now has a caller, safety_core_request_enable(), reached from link_task.c's SAFETY_CMD_REQUEST_ENABLE (0x02) decoder. That path is driven only by an explicit operator/PC command (KilnFW's uart_bridge.c -> safety_link_request_enable(), i.e. PcTools' safety_request_enable MCP tool); KilnFW does NOT request enable automatically when a profile runs, and no scenario in this library models that operator step.
blocked_on.phase: No longer a missing-decoder gap on the SaftyFW side -- link_task.c decodes LINK_FRAME_REQUEST_ENABLE_CMD (0x02) today and relay_owner_command_energize() has its first caller. The remaining gap is on this side of the fence: no scenario issues the operator enable. firmware/SimFW/tools/virtual_dut/dut_core/main.c already accepts an ENABLE command mirroring relay_owner's TRIPPED-refuses / GRACE-defers / ARMED-honours behavior; run_dut_scenarios.py never sends one, because deciding WHEN a scenario would issue it is a scenario-library design question, not something a harness should invent. Owned by SimFW's scenario library, not by SaftyFW.
